subject.title: Feature request: Persistent task-status surface for long-running channel turns

question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent per-channel-turn status surface, and should its canonical owner be channel transport, gateway/session activity, or the task ledger?
rationale: The issue is useful and aligned, but implementation choice determines persistence, restart semantics, channel rollout, config defaults, and whether existing progress/task/status surfaces become competing sources of truth.

options.title: Add a runtime-owned status contract
options.body: Create an additive canonical status model in core/runtime and let Discord project it first as a best-effort editable message.

options.title: Keep current progress drafts only
options.body: Treat progress drafts, status reactions, and task/status commands as sufficient and close or narrow this request to documentation.

options.title: Start with gateway/session activity API
options.body: Resolve the broader activity API first, then build channel projections from that canonical stream in a follow-up.

recommendation.title: Add a runtime-owned status contract
recommendation.body: Create an additive canonical status model in core/runtime and let Discord project it first as a best-effort editable message.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-surface history across Discord progress drafts, status documentation, and task-state movement.
